_: Policy for .github/scripts/dep-audit-gate.mjs. Every exception needs a reason, a whyNotFixed, a reviewTrigger and an expiry date. An expired entry fails the build — that is the point. Do not extend an entry without redoing the analysis; remove it once the underlying fix lands.

exceptions.reason: DoS via brace expansion (unbounded expansion length, exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups, zero-step sequence hang). Dev-tree only, mechanically provable: brace-expansion does not appear in `npm audit --omit=dev`. It is reached through jest only — glob/minimatch@9 in @jest/reporters, and test-exclude/minimatch@3 in babel-plugin-istanbul. The patterns expanded originate from jest's config and this repo's file names, never from untrusted input, and no shipped artifact contains it (build-skill.mjs bundles no node_modules).
exceptions.whyNotFixed: GHSA-mh99 covers <=5.0.7, i.e. every published version except 5.0.8. Forcing `overrides: {"brace-expansion": "^5.0.8"}` breaks the tree: brace-expansion@5 is type:module and exports `expand` as a named export only, while both consumers take the default — minimatch@9.0.9 via `__importDefault(require(...)).default` and test-exclude's minimatch@3.1.5 via `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` called as a function. Measured 2026-07-25 with the override applied: `typeof require('brace-expansion')` returned `object` (namespace, no callable default); minimatch@9 threw `TypeError: (0 , brace_expansion_1.default) is not a function`; minimatch@3 threw `TypeError: expand is not a function`. Notably `npm test` and `npm test -- --coverage` both stayed green — this repo's patterns contain no braces — so the break is real at the API level but unexercised. Shipping a knowingly broken dependency tree to silence a dev-only advisory is the worse trade. Reverted.
exceptions.reviewTrigger: jest's transitive tree reaches minimatch>=10 (which imports the named export): `cd scripts && npm ls brace-expansion --all`. Or a 1.x/2.x backport of the fix is published.

exceptions.reason: Path traversal in serve-static via encoded backslash, Windows only. Pulled in solely by @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's HTTP/SSE transports, which this project never loads: scripts/mcp-bpmn-server.js imports StdioServerTransport only, and scripts/http-server.js uses node:http directly rather than express. serveStatic is never called and there is no Windows deployment path. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is listed alongside @hono/node-server because npm reports it as a separate finding via the effects chain (`via: ["@hono/node-server"]`) — it is the same single advisory, not a second risk.
exceptions.whyNotFixed: The fix requires @hono/node-server >=2.0.5, but @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0 declares "@hono/node-server": "^1.19.9" as a non-optional runtime dependency. npm's only proposed remedy is a semver-major *downgrade* of the SDK to 1.24.3 (`fixAvailable: {"name":"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk","version":"1.24.3","isSemVerMajor":true}`) — there is no forward fix. An override to 2.x would run the SDK outside its declared and tested range in order to patch a code path we never execute.
exceptions.reviewTrigger: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk widens its @hono/node-server range to admit >=2.0.5 (`npm view @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dependencies`), or this project adopts an HTTP/SSE MCP transport — the latter is caught automatically by voidIf below.
